title: Hold the gate
intro: You guard the gate between the plains and the town.
Everything that travels between them passes through you.
The town's notice board must stay open to the citizens. Nothing else is for outsiders.
outro: The gate holds. Scouts found one open door, the garrison alone can manage the board,
and the swarm broke against a limit that follows each source wherever it comes from.

waves.skill: Reading a network: interfaces, routes and listening ports
waves.title: Map the gate
briefing: Nobody attacks yet. Before you can defend the gate you have to know what passes it.
The notice board is the host {web}.
Find out:
- the network on the plains side of the gate
- the network on the town side of the gate
- every TCP port on the notice board that answers from here
Report with:
quest report plains=<network/prefix> dmz=<network/prefix> ports=<port,port,...>
waves.question: Four services answered. How many of them does a citizen reading the board need?

text: A router knows its networks: each of its interfaces sits in one.
A service is a port that answers when you knock.
Look at the gate's addresses and routes with the ip command.
Knock on a range of ports with nc in scan mode. Not every service uses a low port.
ip -br addr          one line per interface, address with prefix length
ip route             the networks as the kernel sees them
nc -zv {web} 1-30000 2>&1 | grep succeeded

questionAnswer: One: the web port. Management, the debug page and the database answered too, and none of them is for a reader.
Every port that answers is a way in. The next waves are about closing the ones nobody outside needs.

waves.title: The scouts
briefing: Scouts on the plains are mapping everything they can reach through the gate.
Right now that is everything: the gate forwards whatever arrives.
Make the notice board's web port ({http}) the only thing an outsider can reach on {web}.
Citizens must still be able to read the board.
Write your rules with nft. When you are ready: quest ready
waves.question: Who else than the citizens needs to reach this server, and for what?

checks.title: The scouts reach the notice board and nothing else
The citizens can read the board

text: A gate that lets through everything that is not forbidden has already lost.
Turn it around: forbid everything, then open what is needed.
The gate has no rules for traffic it forwards.
In nftables that traffic passes a chain on the forward hook. Create one and give it a policy.
Your forward chain accepts by default, so every port you did not think of is open.
Look at the chain's policy.
Your chain drops by default, and that includes the answers.
A request you let in needs its reply let out. Connection tracking knows which packets belong to a flow you already accepted: ct state.
Look at the chain for forwarded traffic and its policy.
Do not forget the replies to flows you have already let in.
Fill in the blanks, save as a file and load it with: nft -f <file>
flush ruleset
table inet gate {
chain forward {
type filter hook forward priority 0; policy ____;
ct state ____,related accept
ip daddr {web} tcp dport ____ accept

answer: type filter hook forward priority 0; policy drop;
questionAnswer: The garrison, which manages the board over port {management}.
A default-deny gate shuts the garrison out too, so the next wave opens that door again, for the garrison alone.

waves.title: The break-in
briefing: The scouts are gone. Now someone is trying to log in to the notice board's management port ({management}),
again and again, from several hosts on the plains.
The garrison manages the board from {garrison} and must keep that access.
Nobody else should be able to reach the management port at all.
Everything from the last wave still has to hold.
When you are ready: quest ready
waves.question: The garrison's address is now a key. What happens the day someone else gets that address?

checks.title: The garrison reaches the management port
Another host on the plains cannot reach the management port
The citizens cannot reach the management port

text: A rule can care about where a packet comes from, not only where it is going.
Open the management port for one source and leave it closed for the rest.
The gate has no forward chain, so the defence from the last wave is gone.
Rebuild it first, then add the garrison.
Match on the source address with ip saddr.
A whole network as source is not one host: every host on the plains shares that network.
Add one rule to your forward chain, above nothing that would drop it first:
ip saddr ____ ip daddr {web} tcp dport ____ accept
nft add rule inet gate forward ...   adds it without reloading the file

answer: type filter hook forward priority 0; policy drop;
ip saddr {garrison} ip daddr {web} tcp dport {management} accept
questionAnswer: An address is easy to borrow: a host on the same network can take it, and simple traffic can be sent from it without owning it.
Real management access needs something only the garrison has as well, such as an SSH key, and ideally a separate management network or a VPN.

waves.title: The swarm
briefing: A flood of web requests is coming at the notice board. First from one host, then from another.
The board is small. Left alone, the flood takes it down for everyone.
No single source may get more than 20 new connections a second through to {web}:{http}.
The citizens ask for a few pages a second and must hardly notice.
Everything from the earlier waves still has to hold.
When you are ready: quest ready
waves.question: Your limit counts per source address. What would an attacker with a thousand addresses do to it?

checks.title: No source floods the board, and the citizens are still served

text: Chasing addresses loses: block one and the flood comes from the next.
Limit how fast anyone may open connections, and count each source on its own.
Nothing in your rules limits a rate yet.
nftables has a limit statement. Used alone it is one shared bucket for everybody, and the flood empties it for the citizens too.
To give every source its own bucket, keep the limit in a set that is filled as sources appear.
You have a limit. Check two things: is it per source address, and is it low enough?
A limit that is shared starves the citizens. A limit above 20 a second lets the flood through.
Inside the table, a set that fills itself:
set flood {
type ipv4_addr
flags dynamic
timeout 30s
In the forward chain, above the rule that accepts the web port:
ip daddr {web} tcp dport {http} ct state new add @flood { ip saddr limit rate over ____/second burst ____ packets } drop

answer: type filter hook forward priority 0; policy drop;
ip saddr {garrison} ip daddr {web} tcp dport {management} accept
ip daddr {web} tcp dport {http} ct state new add @flood { ip saddr limit rate over 10/second burst 10 packets } drop
questionAnswer: Spread the flood over so many sources that each one stays under the limit.
A limit per source stops one loud host. Against many you also need a limit for the service as a whole, filtering further upstream, and a server that can take the load.
